questions.question: Handlebars should be ______ the rider's seat.

options.text: No more than 10 inches higher than
No more than 25 inches higher than

questions.correctAnswerText: No more than 25 inches higher than
questions.explanation: Motorcycle handlebars cannot be more than 25 inches above the rider's seat.

questions.question: When riding with a group of motorcyclists, a staggered formation:

options.text: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
Should be used when riding in curves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should not be used when entering or exiting a highway.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation most of the time. Switch to single-file formation when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger on your motorcycle, you should instruct the passenger to:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle before the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible on the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not talk or move unnecessarily.
questions.explanation: Tell passengers to stay still and quiet while the motorcycle is moving. Passengers should board only after the engine starts. They should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, you should:

options.text: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
Return to your original lane as soon as the truck is behind you.
Return to your original lane when you feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not return to your original lane until you can see the front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Return to your original lane only when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic or pedestrians, and proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn by turning just your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: You approach an emergency vehicle that is stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle begins moving again.
Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge into a lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see an emergency vehicle, tow truck, or roadside assistance vehicle with flashing lights, change lanes to give it space and slow down. Always be ready to stop near an emergency scene.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: Park a motorcycle at an angle of 45 to 90 degrees to the curb. A wheel or fender should touch the curb.

questions.question: When you are being passed on the left, you should:

options.text: Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center portion of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed on your left. Riding on the right side can encourage the other driver to cut back in too quickly.

questions.question: Using all three lane positions is:

options.text: Not encouraged because then you can never get used to any part of a lane.
Discouraged because it confuses other motorists.
Wise if you are adapting to changing conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wise if you are adapting to changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change. No single position is always best or should always be avoided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. This sign warns that the road ahead will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: In broad daylight.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in bright daylight. Always wear bright colors and reflective gear when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When taking a curve while riding in a group, riders should be in:
questions.correctAnswerText: A single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Groups normally ride in a staggered formation. Switch to a single-file line when taking a curve, making a turn, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time, you should:

options.text: Ride more slowly than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your fingers on the clutch and brakes so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Merge
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black words or symbols. This sign warns that traffic ahead will merge into one lane.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To avoid a hazard, press the handgrip on the side where you want to escape.

questions.question: Helmets are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all riders to wear a U.S. Department of Transportation-approved helmet every time they ride. Helmets are the best protection against head and neck injuries.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors. Objects in them look farther away than they actually are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors on your motorcycle.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help maintain control when turning a motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: Accelerate through the turn.
questions.explanation: To stay in control when turning, slow down before the turn. Look in the direction you want to go. Press the handgrip to lean the right way. Gently twist the throttle to stabilize the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a following distance of at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: It is hard to judge distances in the dark. Keep at least three seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead when riding at night.
